newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: REITH URGES SMALL BUSINESS TO WRITE TO OPPOSITION
Federal industrial relations minister Peter Reith has backed away from suggestions his government would use the rejection of unfair dissmissal laws as a trigger for a double dissolution.
On Monday Reith said the government was prepared to go to the polls over its plan to exempt small business from unfair dismissal laws.
But on ABC Radio this morning, Reith backed away from that position, instead urging small business to lobby the opposition to support the new law.
Reith says he would like to see small business people write to the opposition's Bob McMullan and Kim Beazley and demand a fair go for small business by supporting the government's legislation.
BRITISH MP CRITICISES AUSTRALIA OVER NATIVE TITLE
The Australian government has responded to a British Labour MP's criticism of its approach to native title issues.

Norman Godman, a member of two influential parliamentary groups, will urge British foreign secretary Robin Cook to raise concerns about the Howard government's approach to Aboriginal affairs with Canberra.

Speaking after talks in London with an Aboriginal delegation, Godman said many British MP's are growing increasingly concerned about the Federal Government's handling of issues like native title, and its response to the "Stolen Generation" report.

Godman, a Labour MP from Scotland who is a member of the powerful human rights group and the foreign affairs select committee, says he is hoping the British Government will raise those concerns in a friendly way with Australia.
Godman is less than impressed with the Government's response to the Wik decision.
He says Australia's reputation for fair play may be damaged without genuine consultation between the government and Aboriginal groups on native title.
"It seems from all these thousands of miles away that Mr Howard and his colleagues have handled their response to the Wik case in, well putting it mildly, a bloody unsympathetic way," Godman said.
But Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron has described as "a load of old codswallop" Godman's criticism of the government's approach to native title issues.
Senator Herron has told ABC Radio it was clear Godman had heard only one side of the story.
The Minister has rejected claims there has been no consultation with indigenous groups, saying Prime Minister John Howard has had 21 meetings over the Wik issue alone.
SWISS BANKS INVITE CLAIMS FOR HOLOCAUST-ERA ACCOUNTS
Local Jewish community leaders say the decision by Swiss banks to invite claims for accounts that have been untouched since the Holocaust era may be too late.
A man with a Sydney address is among four Australians who appear on a list of 1,000 names published by the Swiss Bankers Association as holders of the dormant accounts.

President of the New South Wales Jewish Board of Deputies Peter Wertheim says while the banks should have made the accounts public long ago, he welcomes the fact there is now a legal basis for lodging claims.
But he believes there is only a slim chance of most of the direct owners of the accounts still being alive.
"I think there would be so few people who would be directly affected by the announcement that most people would regard it as too little too late", Mr Wertheim said.
BURN VICTIM SAMANTHA SAID TO BE COMFORTABLE IN HOSPITAL
A 52-year-old man charged over an attack which left a 10-year-old Townsville girl in hospital with second degree burns has been released on bail.
The man, who is facing one count of grevious bodily harm and two of aggravated assault, will face court in two weeks.
It is alleged a man approached Samantha Green and a group of friends, and threw flammable liquid at them, which was ignited by a candle with which they were playing.
Samantha Green is in a stable condition in Townsville General Hospital and will be assessed by a surgeon today.
The surgeon will decide how to treat the burns Samantha has to her arms and back, equating to 35 per cent of her body.
The hospital says she is resting comfortably after receiving pain relief.
Transporting Samantha to the Royal Brisbane Hospital has been ruled out because her injuries are not serious enough and can be dealt with in Townsville.
Samantha's mother, Veronica, has praised the quick response time of the ambulance service and the hospital's treatment.
Meanwhile, the grandfather of Cairns burns victim Tjandamurra O'Shane has sent his sympathy to the family of Samantha Green.
Patrick O'Shane says he was shocked to hear of the incident, and can not understand the crime.
"I can't understand why people go around picking on kids. This has got me beat, a child hasn't got the mentality of an adult, although some of them have got far more I think", O'Shane said.
MINERS SENT HOME FROM NUMBER ONE MINE ON FULL PAY

In New South Wales, the miners' union says it is dumbfounded that workers at the Hunter Valley Number One Mine were sent home last night and this morning when they returned to work after a six-week strike.
The miners were sent home on full pay.

CFMEU delagete Mick Kelly says workers on last night's dogwatch and this morning's early shift were assembled in a room and told by managers they wanted a "cooling off period" following the dispute over enterprise bargaining.
Kelly says the miners wanted to return to work, and can not understand the company's actions.
Mine manager Alan Davies told ABC radio the miners were sent home because of the tense emotional state currently at the mine.
